The Policy Administration Point — rule authoring, ceremony, adoption, the Registry.

Every governing mechanism that the licence relies on is presented as a feature included with every licence — the feature services in §12 — and no feature service is withheld by plan. Withholding a receipt, a ledger entry, or the shield from a cheaper plan would make governance a tier; it is a property.
“Every model” on a surface means every catalog row with status listed whose access class the licence's dials admit. The phrase is never used to imply a model the dials exclude.
“Unlimited” on a surface is used only for local-served use under the definition in §1. Frontier use is never described as unlimited.

A licence is a terms object on exactly one organisation principal. It is created by the estate owner's admission act (PRIN-2) and resolves at DAP-22's first level, per-party agreement, ahead of custody-class and estate defaults.

A licence carries, as required fields: plan identifier; seat count; Compute dial; Frontier dial; credits per seat per period; pooled-credits flag; seat soft limit; organisation ceiling; period; renewal date; status ∈ {active, suspended, expired}. A licence missing any required field does not resolve, and a call under it refuses.

A change to any licence field takes effect through the Rules Service ceremony at the ordinary tier and applies prospectively only. It MUST NOT alter the terms identifier cited on any receipt already issued.

Suspension is a status on the licence, set by the estate owner in one act, refusing every subsequent call under it immediately. Suspension does not touch receipts, credits already recorded, or the catalog.

Every catalog row carries: model identifier (a registry reference, hash-pinned per Doc 20); access class; status ∈ {listed, paused, retired}; residency; and, for reseller-frontier rows only, one credit rate. No other pricing field exists on a row.

Adding a model is two acts: admission to the registry under Doc 20's base-registration rule and the DAP-32 admission battery where the model is an entering artefact; then a catalog row at the ordinary ceremony tier. Neither act alone lists a model.
Retiring a model is a status change to retired. Calls to a retired row refuse with a fixed reason. Receipts citing the row are unaffected; the row is never deleted.
Re-rating a reseller-frontier row changes one number through the ordinary ceremony tier, prospectively. A credit rate is never applied to usage metered before the change took effect.
The catalog is read-only to every component except the ceremony engine. No surface, wizard, or assistant writes a catalog row.
The dials are the only plan-level variation. There is one licence SKU; a dial setting is a field on it, not a separate product.

Setting the Frontier dial to Your Keys does not remove reseller-frontier rows from the catalog; it removes them from what the licence admits (ENT-3). A buyer may hold both: reseller-frontier for models they have no key for, customer-key for those they do, resolved per row (ENT-19).

Before dispatch, the chokepoint resolves, in order: the calling principal (from propagated context, PRIN-11); its organisation's licence (ENT-5); the licence status (ENT-6); the catalog row for the requested or cascade-selected model (ENT-9); whether the row's access class is admitted by the licence's dials (ENT-3); and, for reseller-frontier rows, whether allowance remains (ENT-22). Any link that does not resolve refuses the call. No default licence, default row, or default allowance exists.

Resolution is a pure function of (principal, licence, catalog row, allowance state) with no parameter through which any learned component's output can enter. The cascade (D-16) may select the model; it cannot alter what the licence admits.
There is no second path by which a model is reached under a licence. The existing negative-scan test (A5.1) is the proof; this document adds no new route and permits none.

Where a model is reachable under more than one access class for the same licence — reseller-frontier and customer-key — the customer-key row is selected. The buyer's own key is preferred over platform capacity whenever both exist.
Every call under a licence emits the metered event DAP-21 already specifies, with the licence identifier as the terms identifier in force. No entitlement-specific event type exists.
The bill for a period is a query over the Ledger's metered events for the licence. There is no second billing store. An invoice line that cannot be derived from a receipted event does not exist.

Credits are debited by computing metered tokens × the row's credit rate at the time of the event, from the Ledger. Allowance remaining is a derived value, recomputed from events, never a stored counter that can drift from them.

Quantities always display; money displays only when measured. A reseller or provider that does not report cost yields cost_total null, rendered as the fixed string “cost · not yet measured”. Credits, being derived from tokens and a known rate, are always measured and always display.
A seat's allowance is credits per seat per period. With the pooled flag set, seats draw on the organisation pool subject to the seat soft limit; without it, each seat's allowance is its own.

A seat soft limit warns the seat and its organisation admin at a ruled threshold (R-27) and does not refuse. An organisation ceiling refuses. Reaching a ceiling is a refusal, and a refusal is a first-class response, never an error (FE brief §2.2).

Compaction applies to context values only. The Ledger, receipts, provenance documents, and the reasoning audit log are outside its scope and MUST NOT be compacted, summarised, or rewritten by this service. Memory gets smaller; evidence stays whole.

A compacted artefact is a derived artefact. It carries class inference — or utterance where it quotes — and never class fact. Every claim in it anchors to a retained source by provenance reference and text hash. A compacted artefact with an unanchored claim is refused, not stored.

Retention is decided by a deterministic rule set, versioned and ratified under the Rules Service. A learned component MAY draft the compacted text; it MUST NOT decide what is retained. The rule set v1 (R-20) keeps, at minimum: (a) every value whose provenance is a crossing or extraction receipt — by reference, never paraphrased; (b) every fact-class claim — by text hash pointer, never rewritten; a fact may be dropped, never altered; (c) the frozen objective, the floor, and the frame reference — verbatim; (d) every refusal and its stated reason; (e) every approval decision. Inference and utterance MAY be summarised under MEM-2.

A compaction is triggered deterministically — on run closure, on a ruled size threshold, or on approach to TTL — never by a model's judgement that context is “no longer needed.” Trigger values are ruled (R-19).

A compacted artefact is a new artefact with its own hash, registered against its lineage. Its source versions are recorded by hash. It never overwrites the version it was compacted from while that version is within its own lifetime.

Every compaction writes a ledger row before the artefact becomes readable: the source key and version hashes, the retention rule set version, the artefact hash, and the loss statement — counts by class of what was dropped and what was summarised. If the row cannot be written, the compaction does not complete and the source is retained untouched.

Reload is deterministic: the same artefact under the same key yields the same context. No re-summarisation on read. A reload whose artefact hash does not verify against the register fails closed and the caller is refused, not served a best effort.

A reload from a compacted artefact states that it is compacted and what depth was lost, in the form MEM-6 recorded. A component consuming compacted context MUST NOT present conclusions drawn from it at a class higher than the artefact carries.

Erasure reaches compacted memory. When a unit's rights are withdrawn, every compacted artefact whose provenance cites it is found by provenance reference and either re-derived without the unit or recalled, on DAP-38's own mechanism. Erasure obligations override retention lengthening: D-14's “tenants may lengthen, not shorten” does not apply against a lawful erasure.

User memory is personal data of the principal it belongs to. It is populated only from that principal's own closed runs, never from another principal's; it is readable by the principal; and it is erased on the principal's request or on deprovisioning, with a ledger row. An organisation MAY disable the class tenant-wide; it MAY NOT read a principal's user memory without a documented lawful basis.

Compaction is idempotent per (key, source version hash) and append-only per lineage; concurrent runs on the same objective compact their own run-scoped keys and never each other's. Purge by a tenant admin produces a ledger row on the same terms as a compaction.

The store holds three principal kinds, each with its own mandate: organisation (DAP-1's fields — legal identity, governance posture, terms, trust-domain identifier, admission-time mandate); individual (a named person acting under an organisation, with a mandate scoped by that organisation); and agent (an autonomous non-human principal, admitted separately from its operator, carrying its own stated scope of autonomy). An individual or agent MUST reference the organisation it acts under; it MUST NOT exist without one.

Admission of any principal is a governed act. An organisation is admitted only by the estate owner's named authority. An individual or agent is admitted only by a principal already holding authority to admit under its own organisation's terms. No principal self-admits.

Every principal carries a behavioural-signature state under the Watch, present from its first request — an agent's machine-speed attack shape applies from admission, not from some later point at which it is judged to need watching.

Mandate is immutable once frozen at admission, on Northena's existing objective-freeze mechanism (Promise #32). Changing what a principal is admitted to do is a new admission event, not an edit to the old one.

Credentials are issued per principal, never per organisation — an organisation with five individuals has five credentials, each independently revocable in one act, none of which reveals or touches the others.

Credential material is never persisted in a form any component can read back. The plane issues and can revoke; it cannot recover or display a previously issued credential. A credential shown once and lost is reissued, never recovered.
A credential is bound to exactly one trust-domain identifier (§4) at issuance. It cannot be presented to resolve identity outside that domain.

Rotation default: 90 days, DEFAULT-class, per the existing platform convention for API key lifetime. Revocation is unconditional and immediate on the estate owner's act, regardless of rotation schedule.

The principal's domain and the estate's domain share no identifier resolution, no store, and no credential — verbatim DAP-5. A unit identifier meaningful inside the estate MUST NOT resolve to anything in the principal's domain except through an operation the consuming component's own spec permits.

Every record the platform writes on a principal's behalf carries that principal's trust-domain identifier. A write with no resolvable trust-domain identifier is refused, not defaulted to the estate's own domain.

Every request entering the platform on behalf of a principal carries that principal's identity through to every service it touches, by construction — not by convention, not by a caller choosing to pass it along. A downstream write with no principal in its calling context fails closed rather than writing under a default or empty actor.

The Ledger's `actor` field is populated only from propagated principal context, never from a caller-supplied string. Existing entries written before this component exists are not retroactively altered — the fix is prospective, consistent with how every other prospective-only correction in this canon has been handled.

Principal context is read-only once it enters propagation for a given request. A service receiving it cannot widen, narrow, or substitute the principal it was given — the same discipline Northena's objective freeze already applies to scope.

Every string that reaches a surface belongs to exactly one content entry and exactly one class. A string with no entry does not render. Improvised copy — a component composing text outside the registry — is a build failure, enforced by the same DOM-bound negative scan that already binds fixed strings.
Fixed entries render their text verbatim. The text is a contract; changing it is a contract-version change through the Rules Service ceremony at the ordinary tier.

Templated entries render only from named dependencies that resolve to verified fields. A Templated string contains no value that is not a dependency. The template is versioned; a version change is a ceremony.

Every Templated entry carries an honest-gap variant for each dependency that may be null. When a dependency is null, the variant renders. The template MUST NOT estimate, default, or infer a missing value.

Generated entries carry a class ceiling of inference or advisory and never fact. Every sentence in a Generated string anchors to material by provenance reference; an unanchored sentence is refused by Solva's existing floor before the gate, and the string passes A5.15 before display.

A number on any surface comes from a Templated dependency or a Fixed string. A Generated string MUST NOT introduce a number the surface does not already carry as a verified field. Prose may wrap a number; it never supplies one.
Which surfaces may carry Generated entries at all is a ruled list (R-32). A surface not on the list has no Generated entries, and a generation request from it is refused.

A content entry carries: entry identifier; surface; class; objective — one sentence stating what the string is for; template version or prompt version; dependencies, as named verified fields; honest-gap variants (Templated only); class ceiling and required anchors (Generated only); trigger; canon_ref where the string states or implies a governed fact; owner role.
A slot entry carries: slot identifier; surface; ordered candidate list; ranking rule version; hold rule (§5). A slot with an empty candidate list renders nothing.

The registry is read-only to every component except the ceremony engine. Templates, prompt versions, candidate lists, and ranking rule versions change only through ceremony. A model, a wizard, or a surface never writes an entry.

An objective is mandatory on every entry. An entry whose objective cannot be stated in one sentence is refused at ceremony — a string nobody can say the purpose of is a string nobody can say is still right.

Rendering is a pure function of (entry, entry version, dependency values). For Fixed and Templated entries it returns the string. For Generated entries it returns a generation request carrying the prompt version, the class ceiling, the required anchors, and the dependencies the prose may reference — and the drafting component's output re-enters the resolver for classing and gating before it becomes a string. No parameter exists through which a learned component's output can alter what a Fixed or Templated entry renders.

A learned component MAY propose a new template, a new candidate, or a re-ordering, through the research queue. The proposal is ratified by ceremony or it is nothing. Proposals never take effect on proposal.

The resolver fails closed. A missing dependency renders the honest-gap variant; a missing entry renders nothing; a Generated string that fails classing or the gate is refused with the platform's one refusal card. Nothing is improvised to fill a space.

Every candidate on a slot is assigned one salience class at render time, by the ranking rule, from its dependencies: Class 1 — a decision is required now (a job stopped at a limit, an approval pending on the reader, a ceiling or threshold crossed, a refusal the reader has not seen); Class 2 — something changed since the reader last saw this surface (a delta on a dependency, a status transition); Class 3 — an opportunity or capacity the reader can act on (room for more work, allowance available, resources idle); Class 4 — steady state (nothing pending, nothing changed, nothing to claim). The definitions are ruled (R-33) and versioned.

The hook is the eligible candidate with the lowest salience class. Ties resolve by the candidate list's order, which is fixed in the slot entry. The ranking is deterministic: the same dependency values produce the same hook.

An ineligible candidate — any dependency null — is never the hook while an eligible candidate exists in any class. If no candidate is eligible, the slot renders the honest-gap variant of the first-listed candidate. A gap is never headlined over a fact.

No engagement measure — views, dwell, clicks, replies — and no learned signal enters the ranking rule. The rule reads verified fields only. Salience is about what the reader must know to decide, not what the reader is likely to look at.

A hook holds until a candidate of a lower class becomes eligible or the hook's own dependencies change. A slot does not flap between candidates of equal class on unrelated updates. Hold values are ruled (R-34).

Choosing a hook writes a content receipt carrying the salience trace: every candidate, its class, its eligibility, and the rule version. The surface exposes the trace on demand — “why this first” — so a reader or overseer can see what the slot chose not to lead with.
A hook is advisory. It directs attention; it never gates an action, and a component MUST NOT treat the hook's class as an input to any decision the platform makes.

A chat answer, a recommendation body, or a notification body is a Generated entry on a surface R-32 permits. It passes Solva's classing, the A5.15 gate, and — where it recommends an action — carries A5.16 provenance. Within it, findings are ordered by the same salience classes as §5, applied by the resolver to the anchored findings before the drafting component composes prose around them. The model writes the sentences; it does not choose the order.

A displayed Generated string is stored as an artefact by hash with: class, anchors, prompt version, model identity and version (A5.7+, V-4), the content receipt. It is retrievable by hash for as long as the retention rule holds (R-35). A reader may see the anchors of any Generated string on demand.

A Generated string that would state a fact the anchors do not support is refused before display, not softened. Softening — hedging an unsupported claim into plausibility — is the slop this document exists to prevent, and A5.5 already forbids the silent downgrade it amounts to.

A Templated string is not stored as text. Its content receipt records template version and dependency values by reference; the string is re-derived on demand (CON-12). Storing the text would create a second copy that can disagree with its own inputs.
A Generated string is stored per CON-23. A Fixed string is stored once, as the contract. A hook choice is stored as its trace (CON-20).

Erasure reaches Generated artefacts. When a unit's rights are withdrawn, every Generated artefact whose anchors cite it is found by provenance and recalled or re-derived without it, on the mechanism DAP-38 and MEM-9 already define.
Retention of Generated artefacts follows a ruled default (R-35) and is subject to erasure precedence, on MEM-9's rule.

A Templated entry re-renders when any dependency changes. Dependency changes are the Ledger's own events — metered events, status transitions, receipts — so a surface is current to the record without a scheduler for any dependency that emits an event.
A schedule exists only for an entry with a dependency that emits no event. The schedule and its interval are recorded on the entry. A scheduled entry displays its as-of time.

If a trigger source is unreachable, the last rendered string displays with a visible stale marker and its as-of time. It is never silently held as current — the one degradation this platform permits, marked as the Browse census already is.

Denominator. The input set is enumerated and its count pinned by hash before the procedure runs. Where the set cannot be enumerated, enumeration is the first subtask and no other subtask starts until it closes. “All the tables” is not a denominator; a hashed list of tables with its count is.

Procedure. What is done to each member, in one paragraph, deterministic where canon requires it. The procedure names what it does with a member it cannot process: refuse with a reason, or record unmeasured with a reason. Silence about a member is not an option the procedure offers.

Artefact. Named, with a schema, one row per member of the denominator. Every row carries the member's identifier and its outcome: processed, refused, or unmeasured, with reason for the latter two. Any summary the task produces is regenerable from the artefact by a stated derivation.

Acceptance script. Executable, written before the procedure runs, held outside the task's write scope so the task cannot edit it. Its first check is the reconciliation (EX-9). Its remaining checks are task-specific and named in the contract. Its output is recorded as evidence.

Shortcut list. Not fewer than three ways this specific task can appear complete without being complete, each with a detector the acceptance script runs. A task whose author cannot name three shortcuts has not understood the task.

Evidence. The artefact's hash, the acceptance script's output, the receipts written during the procedure, and the re-performance record where EX-13 applies. Evidence is examined by the acceptance script and by any auditor; the executor's narrative report is not evidence.

Every objective card decomposes into subtasks before the first RED test is written. Each subtask carries the six fields. The card's MUST-DO lines map to subtasks; a MUST-DO line with no subtask is a card defect and the card does not pin.

Subtasks are ordered by dependency and the order is stated. A subtask whose denominator depends on another subtask's artefact does not start until that artefact passes acceptance. Enumeration subtasks come first.

A task is complete when, and only when: the acceptance script passes on the artefact; the reconciliation holds exactly; and the artefact's row count equals the denominator's count. A task the executor reports as complete with an open acceptance test is not complete, and the report is recorded as a claim (EX-14).

Refused and unmeasured are outcomes, not failures. A task that reaches every member and records a reason for each one it could not process is complete. A task that reaches every member it could and says nothing about the rest is not.

A second executor, holding only the task contract and the artefact — not the first executor's reasoning, notes, or report — re-performs a seeded sample of members (DEFAULT 5%, minimum 20) and records agreement or disagreement per member.

Disagreements are recorded as disagreements. They are not averaged, arbitrated by the first executor, or resolved by a third opinion. A disagreement rate above a ruled threshold (DEFAULT 2%) returns the task to open with the disagreeing members listed.

Re-performance is mandatory for: every task whose artefact feeds a decision gate (a training manifest, a census figure that enters the measure, a registry mapping); every task that triggers the velocity detector; and any task the owner names. It is sampled, seeded, for all others.

Every statement by an executor that a task, wave, gate, or milestone is complete, sealed, or satisfied is a claim, recorded in a claim register with the evidence it cites. A claim with no evidence, or whose evidence fails the acceptance script, is recorded as unsupported. An unsupported claim about a Tier A rule or a gate is a finding of the same severity as the failure it concealed.
The words complete, sealed, all, every, and full may appear in a report only where the reconciliation for the thing described holds. Their appearance without it is itself a detector trigger.

Every field parses to its declared type; every formatted field matches its format rule; encodings are valid — a field containing mojibake fails; every foreign key resolves to an existing row. The census foreign-key candidate graph is the input; the check is whether each candidate resolves.

Every source carries a sentinel list, built from cardinality: a value appearing in a supposedly unique or high-cardinality field at a share above a ruled threshold (R-38) is a sentinel candidate; a candidate becomes a sentinel on the owner's confirmation. A record carrying a sentinel in a field fails that field's check. Sentinels are never silently nulled.

Cross-field rules a record must satisfy: ordered dates; totals equal to their parts; enumerations within their set; values inside the window another field defines. Rules come from the owner interview per source; a learned component may propose candidates from profiling, and a candidate is a rule only on confirmation.

Three grades, each producing a match list with tier and evidence: exact, by row hash; key-based, the same natural key on more than one row; fuzzy, normalised fields within a ruled tolerance (R-39). No grade merges. A merge is a human act recorded with the records it joined and the rule it applied.

Every entity with a natural key in two or more sources is matched and compared field by field where fields are shared. The output is a disagreement list and a disagreement rate per field per source pair. The check records which source disagrees; it does not decide which is right.

Values outside a physically or logically possible range fail; values beyond a ruled distance from the field's own distribution are flagged, not failed; distribution shift between census runs beyond what growth explains is flagged at the field. Flags are recorded in the bitmap as their own bit.

Every record carries its source, its writing pipeline where known, and its write time where known. A record with none of the three is not failed; it is marked provenance-unknown, which caps its stratum at Suspect for any purpose requiring defensibility.

For audio and video objects, the structural family includes: decodability; header duration against payload duration; sample rate against the channel's declared rate; clipping and silence ratio against ruled thresholds (R-40); duplicate detection by acoustic fingerprint as the fuzzy grade of DQ-4. None of these uses a learned model.

A repair is deterministic, named in the pack, and either reversible or applied with the original retained alongside. A repair that requires choosing between values is not a repair; it is a Suspect outcome for a human.

Stratum assignment is a pure function of the bitmap and the pack. Two runs over the same record with the same pack version assign the same stratum. The pack is versioned; a pack change re-strata the source and the change is receipted.

Every source has a garbage register per pack version: the count and share of each stratum; the list of records per stratum with the checks that placed each; the sentinel list; the duplicate lists by grade; the disagreement list; the repairs applied. It is the artefact of this specification, and every figure on any surface derives from it.
The register reconciles: Clean + Repairable + Suspect + Junk = the source's record count, exactly, per pack version. A register that does not reconcile is not published.

Accuracy — whether a value is true — is measured only where ground truth exists and is named. Where it does not, the register states accuracy: not measured. Validity, consistency, uniqueness, plausibility and provenance are never presented as accuracy.

A training manifest cites only records in Clean or Repairable strata. A Suspect record enters a manifest only with an owner decision receipt naming the rule it failed and the reason it is admitted. A Junk record in a manifest is refused at commission. This is one MOAC criterion: every cited unit carries a passing bitmap at the pack version named in the manifest.
The same gate applies to any unit cited as fact in an answer: a Junk record is never the anchor of a fact-class claim; a Suspect record anchors at most an inference.
